steps.reads: One mark in front of the word and the door is doing something. ~ keeps it as a maybe. ? asks about it. ! opens it.
steps.notice: The door never changed. Only how you stand toward it did. Write the mark after the word, door~, and today Spw reads two things: a door, then a thought with nothing to hold. Whether it should bind is an open question.
steps.grow: Mark a word by what it is doing, without rewriting the sentence around it.

steps.reads: Brackets say how you are seeing it: closed. Braces hold what belongs to it, one comma at a time.
steps.notice: Write hinge.frame.key instead and it becomes one long name; the commas are what make three. Four ways to hold: < > what it is about, ( ) where it happens, [ ] how you see it, { } what belongs to it.
steps.grow: Group the parts of one thing so a tool reads them as one.

steps.reads: #> gives the page a name other pages can call. = keeps what you noticed under a word of its own.
steps.notice: A name is a handle: editors list it in the outline and find it from any other file.
steps.grow: Each .spw file in a repository answers to one name; .spw/index.spw routes to them.

steps.reads: @ says from where you are looking. ~ keeps yesterday's page within reach without opening it.
steps.notice: A citation is a path the tools can follow, and they tell you when it breaks.
steps.grow: Link your pages; spw resolve reports every citation as file, route, directory or external.

steps.try: ?["why the same door"]{ !probe{ "count the doors this week" } }
steps.reads: ? opens a question you can come back and close. Inside it, !probe names the small act that would answer it.
steps.notice: A question with a probe is an experiment, not a loose end.
steps.grow: Questions across a repository can be gathered and run; plans keep the answers.
